steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Art, Craft and Design title requires research across MULTIPLE disciplines — not just fine art, but craft and design contexts too.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Understanding different purposes: art (personal expression), craft (material mastery), design (problem-solving) — each discipline has different values and approaches.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Comparing practitioners across disciplines reveals how the SAME theme can be explored through different media, techniques and intentions.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Your research must be CONNECTED to your own work — show how understanding a practitioner's approach has TRANSFORMED your thinking and practice.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring artists craftspeople and designers. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with artists craftspeople and designers. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with artists craftspeople and designers. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to artists craftspeople and designers, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refin | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
